posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: I'm afraid to try to carry laser equipment in a carry on or checked luggage on a plane. Have any of you tried it without getting a major hassle?

posts.author: jsfisher
posts.content_md:
According to the TSA web site regarding lasers:

> You may transport this item in carry-on baggage or in checked baggage. For items you wish to carry-on, you should check with the airline to ensure that the item will fit in the overhead bin or underneath the seat of the airplane.Please be sure to wrap cords tightly around electronics items and pack your bag in neat layers (layer of clothes, layer of electronics, layer of clothes, layer of shoes, etc.) to help officers get a clear look at your bag.Even if an item is generally permitted, it may be subject to additional screening or not allowed through the checkpoint if it triggers an alarm during the screening process, appears to have been tampered with, or poses other security concerns. The final decision rests with TSA on whether to allow any items on the plane.

Given the final paragraph, and especially the final sentence, all I can say is that the TSA website is useless.

posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md: Can you be more specific about the type of equipment?

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: I've carried lasers on in carry-on many times. TSA don't care. Just be ready for them to want to scan it separately.

posts.author: jsfisher
posts.content_md:
Is it generally helpful or not to label the case used to carry the equipment with identifying information? You know, like "Death Ray" and "Effective at altitudes below 55,000 feet".

Ok, I'll get my coat....

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
Possibly things to avoid:

1. Writing something on the case in a non_European language, especially anything that looks like numerals

2. Putting the case down ve-r-r-r-y gingerly and stepping back a few paces

3. Saying things like, "Don't worry about the ticking noise. No, really! Don't worry about it!"

4. Putting a large yellow and black "Radiation" sign on the box.
